auth.signupSub: Sign up to run your shop on Dukaan AI — your data stays private to your account.
auth.demoNote: Accounts are not enabled on this demo deployment. The shop data you see is bundled sample data — no login needed.

auth.err.weakPassword: Password must be at least 6 characters.

settings.title: Settings
settings.lead: Your shop profile, who can work in this shop, language and data.
settings.staffLegacyNote: Staff added before roles were introduced keep Manager access — exactly the access they have always had. Change anyone's role here whenever you are ready.
settings.profileSub: Shown on bills and across the app.
settings.staffOnlyNote: Only the shop owner can change shop settings.
settings.staffSub: People who can work in this shop.
settings.staffSelfNote: You are signed in as staff of this shop. Settings are managed by the owner.
settings.inviteNote: Invite by email and pick a role → the staff member signs up / signs in with that exact email → they land in THIS shop with the access of their role; removing an email cuts access immediately. Manager = full shop access except settings and staff; Cashier = sales, billing, returns and day close only; Accountant = finance, expenses and payments, no selling.
settings.accountSub: Your sign-in details for this shop.
settings.dataSub: Reset demo data restores the sample shop. In production this reseeds the owner's namespace.
settings.confirmBody: All current products, sales and records will be replaced with the sample shop data. In production this reseeds the owner's namespace. This cannot be undone.
settings.acct.title: Money accounts
settings.acct.sub: Where your money sits — the till, wallets and bank accounts. Balances are derived live from the journal; accounts are archived, never deleted.
settings.acct.legacyNote: Holds all history from before money accounts — rename only, cannot be archived.
settings.acct.archiveBlocked: This account carries your pre-accounts history and cannot be archived.
settings.acct.name: Account name
settings.acct.defaultsSub: New payments settle into the default account for their method; the desk can still pick a different account on any payment.
settings.acct.staffNote: Money accounts are managed by the shop owner.
settings.acct.notePlaceholder: e.g. Day's takings deposited to bank
settings.per.title: Fiscal year & periods
settings.per.sub: When your fiscal year starts, and period closing. Once a period is closed, no posting can be dated inside it — corrections are recorded at the correction date, never backdated, exactly as in paper books.
settings.per.lockedThrough: The books are locked through {date}. No posting — sale, expense, bill or correction — can be dated on or before it.
settings.per.notLocked: No period is locked yet. Postings can still be dated on any past day.
settings.per.closeNotePlaceholder: e.g. Month reviewed with the accountant
settings.per.closeConfirm: Lock the books through {date}? This cannot be undone quietly — reopening requires a recorded reason and stays in the history below.
settings.per.errRail: A close cannot cover today or yesterday — offline entries may still be syncing. The latest closable date is {date}.
settings.per.errBackwards: That date is already locked. To move the lock back, use Reopen below.
settings.per.reopenLabel: Move the lock back — locked through
settings.per.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. A missed expense must be entered for last month
settings.per.errReason: A reason is required — every reopening is recorded in the history.
settings.per.reopened: Lock moved back — the books are now locked through {date}.
settings.per.reopenedFully: Periods reopened — no lock is in force.
settings.per.errNothing: There is no lock to reopen.
settings.per.historyEmpty: No period has been closed or reopened yet.
backup.title: Backup & restore
backup.sub: Your whole business in one file — every bill, entry and record. The file is yours: export works in every plan state, always.
backup.exportBody: Downloads one JSON file with the complete business: every collection, the full journal, and this business's own platform records (registry, memberships, counters, events, payments).
backup.exportFailed: The backup could not be prepared. Nothing was changed.
backup.restoreBody: Restore works ONLY into a new, empty business — the books here must be empty. A live business is never overwritten: restore the file into a fresh business and trade there.
backup.restoreSummary: {docs} documents to write ({journal} journal entries) — fingerprint verified against the file's own manifest.
backup.restoreDone: Restore complete — {written} documents written. This business now holds the backup's books.
backup.restoreAlready: This backup is already fully restored here — nothing to write.
backup.restoreFailed: The restore could not be completed. Anything already written matches the backup exactly — pick the same file again to resume.
backup.refused.notABackup: That file is not a Dukaan AI business backup.
backup.refused.unknownFormat: That backup uses a format this version does not know — use a backup exported by this version.
backup.refused.manifestMismatch: The file does not match its own manifest (counts or the journal fingerprint differ) — it may be damaged or edited. Nothing was written.
backup.refused.targetNotEmpty: This business is not empty — restore is refused so a live book is never overwritten. Create a new business and restore there.
backup.ownerOnly: Only the business owner can back up or restore.
dash.lead: Your dukaan at a glance — stock health, today's counter, and what the AI thinks you should do next.
dash.chart.title: Last 14 days revenue
dash.chart.caption: Daily counter totals, oldest to today.
dash.chart.aria: Bar chart of daily revenue for the last 14 days. Total: {total}.
dash.chart.noData: No sales recorded in the last 14 days yet.
dash.top.title: Top products
dash.top.caption: Best sellers by units sold, last 14 days.
dash.top.empty: No sales in the last 14 days yet.
dash.alerts.title: Needs attention
dash.alerts.lowEmpty: Nothing below reorder level. Shelf is healthy.
dash.alerts.expEmpty: Nothing expiring in the next 30 days.
dash.money.title: Money snapshot
dash.activity.title: Recent activity
dash.activity.empty: No bills or expenses recorded yet.
dash.insights.title: AI insights
dash.insights.caption: Computed live from your sales history — no guesswork.
dash.insights.empty: Not enough data yet — record a few sales first.
dash.insight.runOut: {name} will run out in about {days} days at the current rate ({perDay} per day). Suggested reorder: {qty} {unit}.
dash.insight.topSeller: {name} is your star performer — {units} units sold in the last 7 days. Keep its shelf full.
dash.insight.todayVsAvg: Today's revenue is {dir} {pct}% vs your 7-day average of {avg}.
dash.insight.lowCount: {count} items at or below reorder level.
sales.title: Record a sale
sales.subtitle: Pick a product, enter the quantity — the sale is logged and the stock is decremented instantly.
sales.newSaleSub: Works like the shop counter — quick and simple.
sales.searchPlaceholder: Search products — click a result to select…
sales.errStock: Not enough stock — only {qty} {unit} of {name} available.
sales.errRecordFailed: Could not record the sale. Please try again.
billing.title: Billing
billing.subtitle: Scan a barcode or pick items, take split payments — cash, wallet, bank or udhaar — hold bills, print receipts and process returns, all from one desk.
billing.builderHint: A USB barcode scanner works right away — it types the SKU and presses Enter.
billing.skuPlaceholder: Scan or type the SKU, then press Enter…
billing.skuHint: Exact SKU match — Enter adds the item to the bill.
billing.searchPlaceholder: Search products — click or press Enter to add…
billing.resultsHint: Click a product — or use ↑ ↓ + Enter — to add it to the bill.
billing.cartEmpty: No items yet — find a product or scan a SKU to add it.
billing.customerPhonePlaceholder: Needed to send the bill on WhatsApp
billing.errNcName: Enter the new customer's name first.
billing.creditNote: Credit (udhaar) needs a customer name — the unpaid balance ({amount}) lands in the customer's khata automatically.
billing.heldNote: You are completing held Bill #{no} (total {total}). Payments must match that total — or press “New bill” to start fresh and keep it held.
billing.errOutOfStock: Out of stock — only {qty} {unit} of {name} available.
billing.errNoItems: Add at least one item to the bill first.
billing.errItemGone: One of the items is no longer in the inventory.
billing.errQtyZero: Quantity for {name} must be more than zero.
billing.errStockFor: Not enough stock for {name} — only {qty} {unit} available.
billing.availWarn: {name}: only {available} available — {promised} already promised on open orders and challans.
billing.errPayMismatch: Payments add up to {paid} but the bill total is {total}. Adjust the payments so the remaining amount is zero.
billing.errCreditNeedsName: A credit (udhaar) payment needs a customer name — pick a customer or type the name first.
billing.errHeldGone: That held bill is no longer available.
billing.errHeldCompleteFailed: Could not complete the held bill — stock may have changed since it was held. Check the items and try again.
billing.successHeldCompleted: Bill #{no} completed — the receipt is open.
billing.errBillFailed: Could not complete the bill — check the stock and payments, then try again.
billing.successBillCompleted: Bill completed — the receipt is open.
billing.errHoldFailed: Could not hold this bill. Please try again.
billing.successHeld: Bill held — resume it any time from the held bills list below.
billing.successResumed: Resumed held Bill #{no}. Check the payments below, then press “Complete bill”.
billing.returnNote: Any udhaar part of the bill is reduced first; the rest is refunded by the chosen method.
billing.errReturnNone: Enter a return quantity for at least one item.
billing.errReturnMax: Only {qty} of {name} can still be returned on this bill.
billing.errReturnFailed: Could not process the return. Please try again.
billing.successReturned: Return processed for Bill #{no}. Stock and accounts updated.
billing.successVoided: Bill #{no} voided — stock and payments reversed.
billing.historyEmpty: No bills match — completed and held bills show up here.
billing.voidBody: The full {total} will be reversed — stock goes back on the shelf, every payment is returned through its own method, and any udhaar is cancelled. This cannot be undone.
billing.rcpt.thanks: Thank you for shopping with us!
billing.wa.thanks: Thank you for shopping with us!
inv.title: Inventory
inv.subtitle: Every item on your shelf. Rows highlighted in amber are at or below their reorder level — time to restock.
inv.kpi.retailSub: what the shelf would sell for
inv.import.error: Could not read that CSV file. Please check the file and try again.
inv.empty.all: No products yet. Add your first product to get started.
inv.empty.low: No low-stock products. Your shelf is well stocked.
inv.empty.expiring: Nothing is expiring in the next 30 days.
inv.empty.dead: No dead stock. Everything has sold recently.
inv.dead.explain: These items are sitting on the shelf but have not sold in over 60 days — consider a discount or clearing them out.
inv.form.addSub: Add a new item to your shelf.
inv.form.name: Product name *
inv.form.reorderHint: Alert when stock falls to this level.
inv.err.salePricePositive: Sale price must be greater than 0.
inv.err.saleBelowCost: Sale price is below cost price — you would lose money on every sale.
inv.adj.title: Adjust stock
inv.adj.journalNote: Negative adjustments post an inventory write-off at cost to the journal.
inv.adj.error: Enter a quantity change other than 0 (e.g. 5 or -3).
inv.delete.title: Delete product?
inv.delete.body: will be removed from your inventory. Past sales records stay untouched. This cannot be undone.
fc.title: What to order next
fc.subtitlePre: For each fast-moving product we take the
fc.subtitlePost: of units sold, estimate how many days your current stock will last, and suggest a reorder quantity covering 14 days of demand plus a 20% safety buffer.
fc.topSub: Sorted by days of stock remaining — the most urgent first.
fc.empty: No sales history yet — record some sales to unlock forecasts.
fc.howBody1: moving average = units sold in the last 7 days ÷ 7. Days of stock = current stock ÷ moving average. Suggested reorder = ceil(avg × 14 × 1.2 − stock). Slow movers with no recent sales are excluded — ask the
inv.form.taxHint: Leave on Shop default unless this product carries its own rate. Exempt wins over every slab.
inv.form.classHint: Raw materials are bought to be consumed by production (recipes / manufacturing); their stock value is held in the Raw materials account. Goods — including finished products you make — stay in the Inventory account.
inv.form.classReclassNote: Changing the class moves the stock on hand ({amount}) between the Inventory and Raw materials accounts with one reclass entry in the journal. The goods themselves do not move.
sup.title: Suppliers
sup.subtitle: Everyone you buy stock from — what you purchased, what you paid, and what is still payable to each supplier.
sup.empty.none: No suppliers yet. Add your first supplier to start recording purchases.
sup.form.addSub: Add a new supplier to your directory.
sup.form.name: Name *
sup.delete.title: Delete supplier?
sup.delete.body: {name} will be removed from your supplier directory.
sup.delete.bodyCompany: {name} ({company}) will be removed from your supplier directory.
sup.delete.blockedBalance: This supplier still has a payable balance of {amount}. Record the payment first — a supplier with an open balance cannot be deleted.
sup.delete.blockedHistory: This supplier has purchase or payment history, so it cannot be deleted. The history is part of your accounts record.
sup.purchase.title: Record purchase
sup.purchase.sub: From {name}. Stock is increased as soon as you save.
sup.purchase.subCompany: From {name} — {company}. Stock is increased as soon as you save.
sup.purchase.costNote: The latest unit cost becomes the product's cost price.
sup.purchase.errNoLines: Add at least one product line.
sup.purchase.errInvalidLine: Every line needs a product and a quantity above 0.
sup.purchase.errFailed: Could not record the purchase. Please check the lines and try again.
sup.purchase.success: Purchase of {amount} recorded from {name}. Stock increased; payable updated.
sup.payment.title: Record payment
cust.title: Customers
cust.subtitle: Your regulars in one place — how much each customer has bought and how much udhaar is still outstanding against them.
cust.th.name: Name
cust.empty.none: No customers yet. Add your first customer to build the directory.
cust.noteBox: Total purchased counts every completed bill for the customer (held and voided bills are excluded). Credit outstanding comes straight from the udhaar khata.
cust.form.addSub: Add a new customer to your directory.
cust.form.name: Name *
cust.delete.title: Delete customer?
cust.delete.body: {name} will be removed from your customer directory. Past bills and khata entries stay in your records.
cust.delete.blocked: This customer still owes {amount} in udhaar. Collect the repayment first — a customer with an outstanding balance cannot be deleted.
cust.profile.noBills: No bills for this customer yet.
cust.profile.noCredit: No udhaar entries for this customer.
credit.title: Udhaar Khata (Credit Ledger)
credit.subtitle: Who owes you what — udhaar given, repayments received, and the balance still outstanding for every customer.
credit.repay.title: Record repayment
credit.empty.none: The khata is empty. Give your first udhaar to open an account here.
credit.empty.search: No credit accounts match your search.
credit.note.appendOnly: The khata is append-only — mistakes are corrected with an opposite entry, entries are never edited or deleted. Every udhaar and repayment below stays on record exactly as it was written.
credit.notice.given: Udhaar of {amount} given to {name}. Khata updated.
credit.notice.repaid: Repayment of {amount} received from {name}. Khata updated.
credit.field.name: Name *
credit.give.sub: Record a cash loan from the till — money the customer owes you back. For goods sold on credit, use Billing with the Udhaar payment option instead: that records the sale, the stock and the udhaar together.
credit.give.err.customer: Please choose a customer or switch to Walk-in.
credit.give.err.name: Enter the customer's name for a walk-in udhaar entry.
credit.repay.err.exceeds: Amount cannot exceed the outstanding balance of {amount}.
exp.title: Income & Expenses
exp.subtitle: Every shop expense in one register, set against the income it came out of — so the month's real picture is always in front of you.
exp.register.title: Expense register
exp.note.journal: The journal is append-only: editing or deleting an expense posts a reversing entry plus the corrected entry — history is never rewritten.
exp.editNote: Update the expense — a reversing entry keeps the journal honest.
exp.delete.title: Delete expense?
exp.delete.body: {category} — {amount} will be removed from the register. A reversing entry is posted to the journal, so the books stay balanced.
fin.title: Finance
fin.subtitle: Every number below is derived live from the double-entry journal — balances, profit & loss and the cash book can never drift apart.
fin.pl.title: Profit & loss — {month}
fin.pl.caption: Computed from this month's journal entries only.
fin.pl.captionRange: Computed from journal entries in the selected period only.
fin.period.lockedError: That date falls in a closed period (the books are locked through {date}). Nothing can be posted into a closed period — corrections are recorded at today's date instead.
fin.cash.title: Cash book — manual entry
fin.cash.caption: In posts as Owner Capital, Out as Owner Drawings.
fin.cash.notePlaceholder: e.g. Owner added cash to till
fin.export.title: Export data
fin.export.caption: Download CSV files for your accountant or for safekeeping.
fin.export.empty: No journal entries in this range.
fin.export.tallyNote: TallyPrime and Tally ERP 9 accept this standard import file (Gateway → Import Data → Vouchers). Tally versions differ slightly, so import once to validate — the journal CSV carries exactly the same data if your version needs another route.
fin.export.ledgerNamesCaption: If your Tally already keeps a ledger for an account below, write its name here and exports will use it. Only names can change — each ledger's Tally group is fixed, because a wrong group silently distorts the balance sheet.
fin.cb.title: Cash book
fin.cb.caption: Showing the latest 60 entries, newest first. Balance is the running balance of that entry's account right after it posted.
fin.accts.title: Money accounts
fin.chq.title: Cheques
fin.chq.caption: What banks and customers owe the shop in instruments, and what the shop has issued — straight from the ledger's cheque accounts, always equal to the registry's pending totals.
fin.sal.title: Salaries payable
fin.sal.caption: The composition of the salaries-payable account, derived from the journal: what the shop owes its staff, the advances staff owe back, and production labour accrued without a named person.
fin.loan.title: Loans
fin.loan.caption: The loans register's derived position beside the ledger's own balances — the two always agree for loans that have been drawn.
loan.title: Loans
loan.subtitle: Money the shop has borrowed and money it has lent. Outstanding figures derive from the journal and each loan's diary — nothing is stored as a balance.
loan.empty: No loans yet. Create the first loan to start the register.
loan.schedule.title: Instalment schedule
loan.accrue.confirm: Accrue the charge for instalment {n} ({amount})? It posts to the ledger now, as its own entry.
loan.events.title: Loan diary
loan.reverse.confirm: Reverse this event? A mirror entry will be posted — the original stays in the journal.
loan.repay.title: Repayment — {number}
loan.repay.splitHint: The split is attribution: by default charges are settled first. The ledger records the full amount either way.
loan.repay.errAmount: Enter an amount within the outstanding balance, with a split that adds up to it.
loan.form.title: New loan
loan.form.feeHint: Netted from the proceeds at drawdown and recorded as a finance expense. Leave 0 for none.
loan.form.receivableHint: Loans the shop lends are recorded without any charge.
loan.form.errTerms: Check the loan terms: a party, a principal above 0, at least one instalment, and a fee below the principal.
loan.delete.confirm: Delete this unused loan? It has no events and posted nothing.
fin.tax.title: Tax position
fin.tax.caption: Derived from the journal's tax accounts. Tax is a pass-through between your customers, suppliers and the government — it never enters profit & loss.
fin.tax.none: No tax activity yet. Once tax slabs are configured and a taxed sale or purchase is posted, the position appears here.
fin.tax.payCaption: Records a payment against the net tax payable: it reduces Tax payable and leaves from the chosen account.
fin.tax.errExceeds: Amount is more than the net tax payable ({due}).
fin.acct.negative: Negative balance — this account is overdrawn; money went out before it came in.
fin.neg.title: This account will go negative
fin.neg.body: Paying {amount} from {account} will take its balance to {balance}. If this is an informal overdraft you know about, post it anyway.
fin.journal.title: Journal
fin.journal.caption: Every posting, newest first — expand an entry to see its debit and credit lines. Each entry must balance.
fin.fy.title: Fiscal year close
fin.fy.caption: Closing a year moves its income and expense balances into retained earnings in one journal entry and locks the year. Balance-sheet accounts carry forward on their own — the journal is continuous, so there are no opening entries to post.
fin.fy.check.tb: Trial balance for the year balances
fin.fy.check.clearing: Purchases clearing account is zero at year end
fin.fy.check.clearingDetail: Clearing balance {amount} — it nets to zero on every purchase; a balance here means a real defect the close must not bury.
fin.fy.check.draftPayroll: Draft payroll runs inside the year
fin.fy.check.draftPayrollDetail: {count} draft run(s) not yet finalised — they post nothing, but finalise or delete them before closing if the year should carry their salaries.
fin.fy.check.productionDetail: {count} order(s), pool {amount} — work-in-progress carries forward legitimately; this is a warning, not a fault.
fin.fy.check.salaryDetail: Owed to staff {owed} · advances outstanding {advances} · production accruals {unassigned} — carries forward.
fin.fy.check.stockDetail: Ledger {gl} · shelf {shelf} · difference {diff} — a valuation difference, shown for the record; it does not block the close.
fin.fy.openStock.caption: The shelf holds more stock than the books recognise ({amount}) — usually opening stock that was never entered when the shop started on the app. Record it once: Debit Stock, Credit Capital.
fin.fy.openStock.confirm: This posts ONE journal entry dated today: Debit Stock {amount}, Credit Capital {amount}. The journal is append-only — this entry can never be edited or deleted; if the amount is wrong, a reversing entry corrects it.
fin.fy.openStock.posted: Opening stock recorded — the stock book now matches the shelf.
fin.fy.check.lockWill: This close will lock the year — no posting can be dated inside it afterwards.
fin.fy.check.lockAlready: The year is already locked through its last day.
fin.fy.gateBlocked: A hard check above is failing — the year cannot close until it passes.
fin.fy.ackWarnings: I have seen the open items above — close the year with them as they stand.
fin.fy.notePlaceholder: e.g. Closed after the annual stock count
fin.fy.closeConfirmBody: One closing entry will zero the year's income and expense accounts into retained earnings, and the year will lock. This is reversible only by a recorded reopening, which posts a mirror entry — the journal keeps both, forever.
fin.fy.closedNotice: {fy} is closed. Its result now sits in retained earnings; its reports still read exactly as before.
fin.fy.summaryTitle: The year's result — from the closing entry
fin.fy.summaryNetProfit: Net profit carried to retained earnings
fin.fy.summaryNetLoss: Net loss charged to retained earnings
fin.fy.openingsCaption: These are the balances the next year opens with, derived from the journal. No opening entries are posted — a continuous double-entry journal carries every balance-sheet account forward by itself. (Export files for Tally carry these figures as opening balances; the journal never stores them.)
fin.fy.openingsEmpty: No balance-sheet balances carry into this year.
fin.fy.plNote: Reports for a closed year still show its true revenue and expenses: profit & loss reports exclude the closing entry by design, while the trial balance includes it and shows the year zeroed.
fin.fy.reopenReasonPlaceholder: e.g. A supplier bill for June was missed
fin.fy.reopenConfirmBody: A mirror entry will reverse the closing entry to the paisa, the year's accounts will carry their balances again, and the period lock returns to where it stood before the close. The close and this reopening both stay in the journal and the audit trail.
fin.fy.reopenedNotice: {fy} is open again. Remember to close it again when the correction is done.
fin.fy.errNotPast: Only a fully past fiscal year can be closed.
fin.fy.errClosed: This fiscal year is already closed.
fin.fy.errGate: A hard check is failing — see the checklist above.
fin.fy.errWarnings: Tick the acknowledgement for the open items first.
fin.fy.errLocked: The closing entry's date already falls inside a locked period, so the close is refused. Reopen that lock first if this year truly must close.
fin.fy.errNotClosed: This fiscal year is not closed.
fin.fy.errStack: A later fiscal year is still closed. Reopen the later year first — closes unwind in reverse order.
fin.fy.errReason: A reason is required to reopen a closed year.
fin.fy.errInvalid: That fiscal year could not be identified.
tax.title: Tax slabs
tax.sub: Define the taxes your shop charges (e.g. GST). A slab only ever applies when it is active AND set as a shop default below or assigned to a product — until then, no bill or purchase carries tax.
tax.name: Slab name
tax.defaultsSub: The default slab applies to every product that does not carry its own slab. Choose “No tax” to switch tax off for that side — existing bills and purchases never change.
tax.readonlyNote: You can view the tax slabs; only the owner can change them.
dc.title: Day Close
dc.subtitle: Count the cash in the till, compare it with what the books expect, and lock the day in.
dc.alreadyClosed.title: Day already closed
dc.alreadyClosed.text: Today ({date}) was already closed. Saving again will add another close record for today.
dc.close.title: Close today
dc.close.caption: Opening defaults to the last close's counted cash, or the current cash balance when there is no earlier close.
dc.opening.label: Opening cash (PKR)
dc.opening.hint: Cash in the till at the start of the day.
dc.counted.label: Counted cash (PKR) *
dc.counted.placeholder: Count the till and type it here
dc.note.label: Note
dc.note.placeholder: e.g. Short by change given at closing
dc.countedError: Please enter the counted cash from the till.
dc.closedExact: Day closed — counted cash matches the expected cash exactly.
dc.totals.title: Today's auto totals
dc.journalNote: The saved expected cash is the journal figure for {account}; the counter summary above stays as a cross-check.
dc.backlog: Un-closed earlier days: {days} day(s) moved {amount} at the till — already inside today's opening balance; this close records today only.
dc.diff.label: Difference (counted − expected)
dc.history.title: History
ai.title: AI Assistant
ai.subtitle: Ask in Urdu or English — every answer is computed live from your shop's data. Try the starters below.
ai.error: Sorry, something went wrong while answering. Please try again.
ai.note: Answers are grounded in your shop data. On the live deployment a Gemini-powered assistant (via /api/chat) answers first; the on-device intent engine covers everything else — no key, no network, no problem.
doc.estimateNote: Estimate only — agreed prices and discounts hold; tax is fixed by the bill when the sale is made.
doc.lines.searchPh: Search products — click or Enter to add…
doc.agreedPrices: Agreed prices from the order apply.
doc.errNoLines: Add at least one item first.
doc.errQtyZero: Every item needs a quantity above zero.
doc.errPriceZero: Every item needs a price above zero.
doc.errNotEditable: Only a draft can be edited — an issued document is a promise. Cancel it and issue a new one to change it.
doc.errConvertState: This document can no longer be converted.
doc.errCancelBlocked: This document already has fulfilled quantities, so it cannot be cancelled.
doc.errNothingRemaining: Nothing remains to convert on this document.
doc.cancelConfirmBody: {label} will be marked cancelled. It never posted anything, so no accounts change.
doc.deleteConfirmBody: The draft will be removed. Drafts carry no number and post nothing.
quote.title: Quotations
quote.subtitle: Priced promises to customers. A quotation posts nothing — no stock, no udhaar, no journal — until it converts.
quote.form.sub: Saving keeps this a draft. It receives its QT number only when issued.
quote.empty.none: No quotations yet. Create one to quote a customer a price before selling.
quote.notice.draftReadyBill: Bill draft for {number} is ready at the billing desk — complete the payment there to post it.
order.title: Sale Orders
order.subtitle: Confirmed orders at agreed prices. An order posts nothing itself — converting it prepares a bill at the billing desk.
order.form.sub: Saving keeps this a draft. It receives its SO number only when confirmed.
order.empty.none: No sale orders yet. Create one directly, or convert an accepted quotation.
order.notice.draftReady: Bill draft for {number} is ready at the billing desk — complete the payment there to post it.
challan.title: Delivery Challans
challan.subtitle: Delivery notes for goods leaving the shop. A challan posts nothing and moves no stock — the bill does that when the delivery is charged.
challan.form.sub: Saving keeps this a draft. It receives its DC number only when dispatched.
challan.quantitiesOnly: Quantities only — this is a delivery note, not a bill.
challan.deskNote: Billed at the order's agreed prices where the challan cites one; otherwise at the challan's own prices.
challan.empty.none: No delivery challans yet. Create one for a delivery, or convert a sale order.
challan.notice.draftReady: Bill draft for {number} is ready at the billing desk — complete the payment there to post it.
challan.notice.fromOrder: Challan draft created from {number} — add dispatch details, then dispatch it.
challan.errOrderGone: The source order can no longer send goods out.
po.title: Purchase Orders
po.subtitle: Orders placed with suppliers at agreed costs. A purchase order posts nothing — stock and the supplier's payable move only when goods are received against it.
po.form.sub: Saving keeps this a draft. It receives its PO number only when issued.
po.receiveSub: Quantities start at what is still outstanding, at the order's agreed costs — correct a cost to the supplier's actual invoice where it differs. Receiving posts the goods through the ordinary purchase book; the purchase cites this order.
po.printNote: Order at agreed costs — tax is fixed when the goods are received.
po.empty.none: No purchase orders yet. Create one to order stock from a supplier.
po.notice.received: Goods received against {number} — the purchase is recorded in the supplier's book.
po.errOverReceipt: A quantity exceeds what is still outstanding on this order — receiving more than was ordered is refused.
po.errReceive: These goods could not be received against this order.
settings.docSeriesSub: The prefix each document series is numbered with. A change applies to documents numbered from now on; numbers already issued never change.
quote.wa.title: Quotation {number} — {date}
note.title: Credit & Debit Notes
note.subtitle: The formal paper for returned goods. A credit note is minted with a bill return; a debit note with goods returned to a supplier. Every note wraps a posting that is already in the ledger — the note itself never moves money.
note.empty: No notes yet. Post a formal bill return or return goods to a supplier and its note will appear here.
note.issue.title: Issue credit note
note.issue.sub: Post a return against a posted bill — the return posts through the ordinary returns engine and the credit note is minted with it, in the same step.
note.issue.noBills: No posted bills can take a return right now.
note.issue.reasonPh: Why are the goods coming back?
note.issue.failed: The return could not be posted.
note.print.footer: This note formalizes a return already posted to the shop's ledger.
sup.preturn.title: Return goods to supplier
sup.preturn.success: Debit note {number} issued — the goods are returned.
sup.preturn.failed: The purchase return could not be posted.
sup.preturn.none: Enter a return quantity for at least one item.
sup.preturn.errMax: Only {qty} of {name} can still be returned.
chq.title: Cheque Registry
chq.subtitle: Every cheque the shop has received or issued, through its whole life — captured with a payment, deposited, cleared or bounced. The registry is the instrument's diary; the money itself always moves through the ledger.
chq.searchPh: Search cheque number, bank or party…
chq.empty: No cheques yet. Choose Cheque in a bill, an udhaar repayment, a supplier payment or an expense and it will appear here.
chq.err.capture: Enter the cheque number, bank and both dates first.
chq.deposit.title: Deposit cheque
chq.deposit.hint: Depositing is a custody move only — no money moves yet. The amount lands in the chosen account when the cheque clears.
chq.clear.title: Mark cheque cleared
chq.clear.hintIn: The bank has paid — the amount lands in the deposit account now.
chq.clear.hintOut: The bank has paid — the amount leaves the drawn-on account now.
chq.bounce.title: Cheque bounced
chq.bounce.hintIn: The amount becomes owed by the customer again — it re-opens on their udhaar, against the original bill where there is one.
chq.bounce.hintOut: The amount becomes owed to the supplier again.
chq.return.title: Return cheque to customer
chq.return.hint: The cheque is handed back undeposited — the amount becomes owed by the customer again. Take the replacement as an ordinary repayment afterwards.
chq.notice.failed: That action could not be completed.
rep.title: Reports
rep.subtitle: Every figure in the shop, on paper: sales, purchases, stock, profit, tax, statements and more — the same numbers the screens show, ready to save, print and share.
rep.snapshotNote: This report shows the current position — the date range does not apply to it.
rep.sales.title: Sales Report
rep.sales.desc: Period totals, best-selling products and sales by customer — returns netted exactly as the Sales screen nets them.
rep.purchase.title: Purchase Report
rep.purchase.desc: What came in during the period, by supplier and by product, net of purchase returns.
rep.stock.title: Stock Report
rep.stock.desc: Current stock with its value at cost, the low-stock list and what expires within 30 days.
rep.pl.title: Profit & Loss
rep.pl.desc: Revenue, cost of goods, expenses and net profit for the period — the Finance screen's own computation.
rep.cashbook.title: Cash Book & Account Statement
rep.cashbook.desc: Money in and out for one account (or the whole cash book), with opening and closing balances.
rep.tax.title: Tax Report
rep.tax.desc: Output tax collected on sales and input tax paid on purchases, slab by slab, and the net position.
rep.customer.title: Customer Statement
rep.customer.desc: One customer's khata: opening balance, udhaar given, repayments and the closing balance.
rep.supplier.title: Supplier Statement
rep.supplier.desc: One supplier's account: purchases, payments, purchase returns and the closing balance.
rep.aging.title: Aging — Receivables & Payables
rep.aging.desc: Who owes the shop and whom the shop owes, aged 0–30, 31–60 and over 60 days — identical to Finance.
rep.expenses.title: Expenses Report
rep.expenses.desc: Every expense of the period, grouped by category.
rep.cheques.title: Cheques Report
rep.cheques.desc: Cheques captured in the period, grouped by where they stand: drawer, bank, issued, cleared, bounced.
rep.dayclose.title: Day Close Summary
rep.dayclose.desc: The recorded day closes inside the period, with their counted and expected cash.
rep.notes.title: Credit & Debit Notes
rep.notes.desc: The formal notes issued in the period — credit notes to customers, debit notes to suppliers.
rep.tb.title: Trial Balance
rep.tb.desc: Per-account debit and credit totals from the journal for the period, with closing balances — the difference must be zero.
rep.tb.balanced: Balanced — total debits equal total credits
rep.bs.title: Balance Sheet
rep.bs.desc: What the shop owns and owes as at the end of the period, from the journal: assets on one side, liabilities, capital and the unclosed result on the other — the two sides must be equal.
wh.title: Warehouses
wh.subtitle: The places your stock sits. Every product's total is split across these warehouses; sales, purchases and adjustments each record the warehouse they touched. Stock value is always at the product's one cost price — a warehouse is a place, not a separate business.
wh.form.name: Name
wh.notice.archived: Warehouse archived. Its stock history stays readable.
wh.cannotArchiveDefault: The default warehouse cannot be archived — make another warehouse the default first.
wh.empty: No warehouses yet. Add one to split your stock by location.
wh.stockEmpty: Nothing is stocked at this warehouse yet.
wh.drift.title: Location split needs a recount
wh.drift.body: {count} product(s) have warehouse quantities that no longer add up to their totals — this happens when an older version of the app recorded stock without locations. Your totals and accounts are correct; only the split needs repair.
wh.drift.done: Recount complete — {count} product(s) repaired. No accounts were touched.
wh.drift.item: {name}: locations add up to {rows}, total is {total}
tr.title: Stock Transfers
tr.subtitle: Move stock between your own warehouses. Dispatch takes the goods off the source shelf and puts them on the road; receiving lands them at the destination. A transfer moves no money — only a shortage proven at closing posts to the accounts, as a stock loss.
tr.empty: No transfers yet. Create one to move stock from one warehouse to another.
tr.lines.searchPh: Search products — click or Enter to add…
tr.lines.empty: Add at least one product to move.
tr.err.same: Source and destination must be different warehouses.
tr.err.route: Both warehouses must exist — refresh and try again.
tr.err.archived: An archived warehouse cannot send or receive new transfers.
tr.err.overReceive: A line cannot receive more than was sent. Check the quantities.
tr.notice.dispatched: {number} dispatched — the goods are on the road.
tr.notice.closedShort: {number} closed — a shortage of {amount} was booked as a stock loss.
tr.notice.returned: {number} closed — what was still on the road went back to {name}.
tr.receive.title: Receive goods — {number}
tr.receive.help: Enter what actually arrived this time. Anything left stays on the road and can be received later — or closed as a shortage.
tr.close.title: Close with shortage — {number}
tr.close.body: These goods were sent but never arrived. Closing books them as a stock loss at today's cost — this is the one transfer action that posts to the accounts, and it cannot be undone.
tr.return.title: Return to source — {number}
tr.return.body: The {qty} unit(s) still on the road go back onto the shelf at {name}. Goods already received stay where they are.
tr.print.title: Stock Transfer
tr.print.quantitiesNote: Quantities only — a transfer moves stock between your own warehouses; no value changes hands.
mfg.title: Manufacturing
mfg.subtitle: Recipes (BOMs) for the products you make: what one batch consumes, what it yields, and what a finished unit costs. Recipes never post anything — production does, when it runs.
mfg.immutableNote: A recipe is never edited in place. Saving a change creates a new version and the old version stays readable forever, so a production order always shows the exact recipe its costs came from.
mfg.empty: No recipes yet. Add one for a product you make — a repack, a blend, an assembly — and production can run against it.
mfg.raw.title: Raw materials on the shelf
mfg.raw.sub: Products classed as raw material — their stock value sits in the Raw materials account and recipes consume them. Set a product's class in Inventory.
mfg.po.title: Production orders
mfg.po.sub: Run production against a recipe: issue materials into work-in-progress, land finished units at their absorbed cost, and write off what spoils.
mfg.po.empty: No production orders yet. Create one from a recipe to start making a product.
mfg.po.snapshotNote: Recipe snapshot — version {v}. Later recipe versions never change this order's costs.
mfg.po.form.title: New production order
mfg.issue.title: Issue materials — {name}
mfg.issue.makeDefault: Remember this settlement as my default
mfg.complete.title: Record completion — {name}
mfg.complete.final: Final completion — absorb the whole remaining cost pool
mfg.scrap.title: Record scrap — {name}
mfg.close.confirm: Close this order? The remaining in-progress value of {amount} will be written off to loss.
mfg.close.confirmEmpty: Close this order? Nothing remains in progress for it.
mfg.print.title: Production order
mfg.err.outputRaw: A raw material cannot be a recipe's finished product.
mfg.err.selfComponent: A product cannot be its own component.
mfg.err.badQty: Every component needs a quantity above zero.
mfg.err.badBatch: Batch size must be above zero and costs cannot be negative.
mfg.err.generic: This recipe could not be saved.
mfg.po.err.generic: This production action could not be saved.
mfg.po.err.insufficient: Not enough {name} at the order's warehouse.
mfg.po.err.emptyPool: Nothing is in progress for this order — issue materials first.
mfg.po.err.noAccount: No money account is available for the payment.
mfg.po.err.zeroValue: This issue would move no value — give the run materials or conversion costs.
mfg.po.err.notOpen: This order is closed to further events.
mfg.po.err.outputGone: The finished product no longer exists.
job.title: Job Tracker
job.subtitle: Customer work orders — printing, binding, made-to-order work — tracked from receipt to delivery: materials issued to the job, advances held in the customer's pool, and the bill that settles it.
job.empty: No jobs yet. Take a customer's work order — the job is born with its number, ready to go on the customer's slip.
job.noAdvances: No advances recorded for this job.
job.form.name: Customer name
job.form.title: Work title
job.form.errTitle: Give the job a title — the work, in a few words.
job.form.errWarehouse: That warehouse is no longer available.
job.form.errSave: The job could not be saved. Nothing was written.
job.form.warehouseLocked: The warehouse is fixed once materials have been issued to the job.
job.mat.err.not_active: This job is closed — materials no longer move on it.
job.mat.err.unknown_product: A picked product no longer exists.
job.mat.err.bad_qty: Quantities must be greater than zero.
job.mat.err.insufficient: Not enough stock at the job's warehouse for {name}.
job.mat.err.over_return: The job holds only {qty} of {name} to return.
job.mat.err.zero_value: These materials carry no cost — there is nothing to post.
job.mat.err.failed: The materials could not be posted. Nothing was written.
job.adv.title: Record advance — {number}
job.adv.sub: An advance is ordinary money in against this customer's future bill — it sits in the customer's pool and the job's bill absorbs it when posted.
job.adv.errAmount: Enter an amount greater than zero.
job.adv.errFailed: The advance could not be recorded. Nothing was written.
job.notice.draftReady: Billing job {number} — compose the charge lines. Materials already issued to this job are listed below and must not be billed again.
job.bill.materialsSub: These goods already left the shelf and were charged to the job's cost — do not add them as bill lines again.
job.print.title: Work slip
job.stages.title: Job stages
job.stages.sub: The workshop stages a job moves through — one per line, in order. A new job starts at the first; reaching the last marks it Ready. Jobs keep the stage name they already carry if you rename the list.
staff.title: Staff
staff.subtitle: Everyone who works here — their terms, their attendance, and what the journal says they are owed. Employees are not logins: most staff never sign in, and their records live here, not in Settings.
staff.th.name: Name
staff.empty.none: No employees yet. Add your first team member to open the directory and the attendance register.
staff.noteBox: Positions are read from the double-entry journal (salaries payable, per employee) — never typed in. Deactivated staff keep their full history and can be reactivated any time.
staff.form.addSub: Identity and current pay terms. A raise edited here changes future payroll runs only — posted runs keep their snapshots.
staff.form.editSub: Terms are the employee's CURRENT terms; runs already posted keep the terms they snapshotted.
staff.form.name: Name
staff.form.paidLeaveHelp: Monthly basis only: absences within this allowance do not reduce the salary; beyond it, pay is docked pro-rata over the month's days. Daily-basis staff are paid per day present.
staff.form.linkedEmailPh: Only if this person also signs in
staff.form.linkedHelp: Informational only — it grants no access and gates nothing. Logins and roles are managed in Settings.
staff.err.baseInvalid: Enter the pay amount (0 or more).
staff.delete.title: Delete this employee?
staff.delete.body: “{name}” has no attendance, payroll, loan or journal records, so the directory entry can be removed. This cannot be undone.
staff.delete.blocked: This employee has records (attendance, payroll or journal entries), so they can only be deactivated — history is never deleted.
staff.profile.attendanceThisMonth: This month so far: {present} present · {absent} absent · {half} half · {leave} leave
staff.profile.payrollNote: Salary accruals, advances and payments join this position as payroll runs are posted; the figures above are always derived from the journal, never stored.
att.title: Attendance register
att.subtitle: Tap a day to cycle its mark. The register records time only — it never posts money; payroll reads it when a run is composed.
att.legend: Marks: P present · A absent · H half day · L leave · O weekly off. One tap cycles to the next mark; tapping an off day clears it back to unmarked.
att.postedWarning: A payroll run for this month is already posted. Editing these marks changes no posted slip — it would only change a re-run, which the payroll reversal flow governs.
att.empty: No active employees yet — add staff in the Directory tab and the register opens for them.
att.help: Unmarked days stay blank: the register never assumes a day was worked.
pay.title: Payroll runs
pay.subtitle: One run per month: composed from the register, finalised into the journal as a single net accrual, then paid in cash or bank. Corrections are reversals — a posted run is never edited.
pay.empty.none: No payroll runs yet. Compose the first run for a month — it starts as a draft and posts nothing until you finalise it.
pay.editor.title: Run for {month}
pay.editor.caption: Lines were composed from the attendance register and each employee's current terms. Adjust allowances or add deductions — the figures you finalise are exactly what posts. Absence beyond paid leave is already inside the earned base.
pay.finalise.confirmBody: This posts ONE journal entry: salary expense {net} against salaries payable, per employee at net. The run can afterwards only be corrected by reversing it. Payments are recorded separately as salaries are handed out.
pay.finalise.postedMonth: A posted run already covers {month}. Reverse it first if the month must be re-run — two accruals for one month would double the expense.
pay.finalise.nothing: Nothing accrues in this run (every line nets to zero), so there is no entry to post.
pay.reverse.confirmBody: A mirror entry undoes the accrual and the run reads Reversed; the month can then be re-run. Payments already made STAND — the money really moved — and now sit as advance positions for those employees.
pay.detail.caption: Accrued, advanced, paid and still owed — every figure derives from the journal and this run's payment events; nothing here is typed in.
pay.payments.title: Payments
pay.bucket.title: Production labour awaiting payment
pay.bucket.caption: Production orders accrued {amount} of labour and overhead to salaries payable without naming a person (the order, not the worker, was the record). Pay it here against any posted run; the ledger total falls the same either way.
pay.pay.title: Pay salary
pay.pay.remaining: Still to pay on this run: {amount}
pay.pay.errAmount: Enter an amount above zero and no more than what is still owed.
pay.advance.title: Salary advance — {name}
pay.advance.caption: An advance is money ahead of earnings: it debits the employee's salary position, never an expense. It is recovered from future salary by derivation — the next run's slip shows the recovery.
pay.advance.errAmount: Enter an advance amount above zero.
pay.notice.finalised: {number} finalised — the accrual is in the journal.
pay.notice.paymentReversed: Payment reversed — the mirror entry is in the journal.
pay.notice.runReversed: {number} reversed. The month can be re-run.
pay.casualHint: Casual day labour that is NOT on this directory is still paid from Expenses (salary category). A person on payroll must be paid through payroll, or their pay double-counts.
pay.history.title: Salary history
pay.history.empty: No payroll runs cite this employee yet.
slip.title: Salary slip
print.title: Print & branding
print.sub: How bills and documents look on paper — paper, header, item columns and footer. Until you change anything here, printing stays exactly as it is today.
print.headerModeNote: Letterhead and logo images are added under Brand assets; until an image exists, the text header prints.
print.colTaxNote: Bills and notes only — quotations and orders carry estimates, never per-line tax.
print.footerNotePh: Printed at the end of bills and documents
print.termsPh: Your terms, printed small in the footer
print.thanksPh: Leave empty for the standard line
print.brand.title: Brand assets
print.brand.sub: Your logo, letterhead, stamp and signature, printed on bills and documents. Images are compressed automatically on this device and stored with your shop.
print.brand.logoHint: Shown in the header when the design calls for it. A transparent PNG works best.
print.brand.letterheadHint: A full-width banner image. On thermal 80mm prints the text header is used instead — banners never print on thermal.
print.brand.stampHint: A transparent PNG prints like a real stamp impression.
print.brand.signatureHint: Replaces the ruled signature line on the documents you choose below. A transparent PNG works best.
print.brand.raastNote: The QR your bank gave you, saved from your banking app. It prints with Raast payments once Raast is set up (Payments).
print.brand.tooLarge: This image compresses to {actual} KB — over the {cap} KB limit. Crop it or use a simpler image, then try again.
print.brand.badType: That file could not be read as an image.
print.raast.title: Payments — Raast QR
print.raast.sub: Print a Raast QR on bills so customers can scan with any banking app and pay straight to your account.
print.raast.honest: Two ways, honestly labelled. Your bank's own QR image (uploaded under Brand assets) is the verified path — when it exists, it prints. The code generated here follows the State Bank's published person-to-person (P2P) template, built from your IBAN alone. It is not a bank-issued merchant (P2M) code — only your bank can issue one of those — and the generated code has not yet been verified against a real bank Raast QR, so scan-test it with your own banking app before you rely on it.
print.raast.provisional: Generated QR: pending verification against a real bank Raast QR.
print.raast.ibanHint: Your IBAN is printed on your cheque book and shown in your banking app under account details.
print.raast.fiHint: As your bank prints it — up to 25 characters.
print.raast.err.alias: A mobile number cannot be used here — the Raast QR standard carries an IBAN, not a phone alias. Your IBAN is on your cheque book and in your banking app.
print.raast.err.notPk: Only a Pakistani (PK) IBAN works with Raast.
print.raast.err.length: A Pakistani IBAN is exactly 24 characters — a character seems missing or extra.
print.raast.err.format: The middle of an IBAN is a 4-letter bank code followed by the account number. Copy it exactly as printed.
print.raast.err.checksum: The IBAN's check digits do not match — a digit is wrong somewhere. Copy it exactly from your cheque book or banking app.
print.raast.err.fi: The bank name must be at most 25 characters, in English letters as your bank prints it.
print.raast.validNote: This IBAN checks out. Before relying on it, scan the preview with your banking app and confirm YOUR name and account appear.
print.raast.pathImage: On bills: your bank's QR image prints (Brand assets) — the verified path.
print.raast.pathGenerated: On bills: the generated Raast code from this IBAN prints.
print.raast.pathNone: On bills: no Raast QR yet — save an IBAN here, or upload your bank's QR image under Brand assets.
print.raast.showToggle: Print a Raast QR on bills
print.raast.dynamicToggle: Put the bill's amount and number in the QR (dynamic)
print.raast.dynamicNote: The code carries the bill total, so the customer just scans and pays — and the bill number lets you match the payment later. Quotations always carry a plain code with no amount: an estimate is not a demand.
print.raast.posterNote: One static code for the counter — the customer scans and types the amount.
print.raast.sampleNote: A test IBAN for the demo, shown only so you can see the code. It never prints on a real bill.
print.raast.caption: Scan with any banking app to pay via Raast
pin.title: This device's lock
pin.honesty: The PIN keeps this device's app private from casual use at the counter. It is not a replacement for your account password — anyone who knows the account password can remove the PIN. Your shop data stays protected by your account sign-in.
pin.statusNone: No PIN is set on this device — the app opens here without a PIN.
pin.statusSet: A PIN is set on this device since {date}.
pin.errMismatch: The two PINs do not match.
pin.errCurrent: That current PIN is not correct — nothing was changed.
pin.errPassword: That account password was not accepted — nothing was changed.
pin.gate: Ask for the PIN before sensitive actions
pin.gateSub: Voiding a bill, submitting the day close, and closing or reopening a period or fiscal year will ask for this device's PIN first — only on this device, and only while a PIN is set.
pin.demoRecovery: There is no password in demo mode: if this PIN is forgotten, the lock screen can erase the demo data and remove the PIN.
pin.lock.paused: Too many wrong tries. The pad opens again in {sec} seconds.
pin.recover.title: Forgot the PIN?
pin.recover.body: Enter the password of the account signed in on this device. The PIN is removed, the app opens, and you can set a new PIN in Settings. Forgetting the PIN never locks you out of your own shop.
pin.recover.failed: That password was not accepted — the lock stays on.
pin.demoErase.title: Erase demo data and remove the PIN
pin.demoErase.body: There is no account password in demo mode. Erasing resets the demo shop to its sample data and removes this device's PIN.
pin.demoErase.typeLabel: Type the shop name to confirm
pin.gate.title: PIN required
pin.gate.body: Enter this device's PIN to continue.
pin.gate.actFiscal: Close or reopen the fiscal year
loyalty.title: Loyalty Points
loyalty.subtitle: Points your customers have earned and not yet spent. Every point is a rupee the shop owes — earned, spent, returned and expired points all move through the ledger, so this page always agrees with your books.
loyalty.off: The loyalty programme is switched off in Settings. Existing balances stay here — customers can still spend them, and expired points can still be posted.
loyalty.expiredSub: These points passed their expiry date. They still count in the liability above until you post the release — posting moves them out of the liability and back against the programme's cost. Nothing expires on its own.
loyalty.empty: No customer has loyalty points yet. Points are earned automatically on a named customer's bill while the programme is on.
bill.pointsMaxNote: Up to {cap}% of this bill can be paid in points.
bill.walkinNoEarn: Walk-in bills don't earn loyalty points — add the customer to earn.
bill.pointsNeedsCustomer: Points can only be used on a named customer's bill.
rep.loyalty.title: Loyalty points
set.loyalty.title: Loyalty programme
set.loyalty.sub: Reward repeat customers with points. Points are a liability in your books: earned points cost the programme account, spent points pay part of a bill, and expired points are released only when you post them from the Loyalty page.
set.loyalty.earnBase: Rupees of a bill per point earned
set.loyalty.redeemCap: Most of a bill payable in points (%)
set.loyalty.silverAt: Silver tier — points earned in a year
set.loyalty.goldAt: Gold tier — points earned in a year
set.loyalty.note: Tiers only make points accumulate faster — a point is worth the same rupees for every customer. Switching the programme off stops new points; balances already earned stay spendable and expirable.
biz.noAccessBody: This account does not belong to any business right now. If you were removed from a shop, its owner can invite you again.
biz.createBody: A new, empty business on the Free Trial plan. Your current business is untouched.
biz.createFailed: Could not create the business. Please try again.
biz.setupIncomplete: This business is still being set up.
plan.trialBanner: Free trial — {days} days left, {left} invoices remaining of {limit}
plan.graceBanner: Your plan ended {days} days ago. You can view, print and export everything, but new entries are paused until renewal.
plan.readonlyBanner: This shop is read-only: the plan's grace period has ended. Your data stays safe and fully viewable.
plan.suspendedBanner: This shop has been suspended by the platform. You can still view all your data.
plan.lockedBody: This feature is part of the {tier} plan and above. Your current plan is {plan}.
plan.limitInvoices: Invoice limit reached for this period ({limit}). Posting resumes next period or after an upgrade.
plan.limitMembers: Your plan allows {limit} users. Remove a member or upgrade to add more.
plan.postingPaused: Posting is paused while the shop is {state}. You can still view, print and export.
plan.panel.title: Plan & usage
plan.panel.enforceOn: Enforcement is ON for this shop
plan.panel.enforceOff: Enforcement is off — usage is being observed only
renew.title: Renew or upgrade
renew.intro: Pay the platform by transfer, then submit the record here. Your new period starts when the platform confirms the payment — from the later of your current period's end and the confirmation.
renew.billing.annual: Annual — 12 months for the price of 10
renew.instructionsNone: Payment instructions have not been published yet — please contact the platform before paying.
renew.referenceHint: Shown in your banking app or on the slip
renew.submit.done: Submitted. The platform confirms after checking the transfer; your period extends at confirmation.
renew.submit.failed: The submission failed — nothing was recorded. Please try again.
renew.error.referenceRequired: Enter the transaction reference first — the platform checks it against the transfer.
renew.error.quoteChanged: The amount or period changed — review the figures, then submit again.
renew.pay.confirmedPeriod: Confirmed — your plan now runs to {date}.
renew.pay.rejectedHint: You can pay again and submit a new record.
renew.enterpriseNote: Enterprise terms are arranged directly with the platform — this plan's renewals are handled by the platform team.
renew.banner.trialApproaching: Your free trial ends in {days} days — renew now so posting continues without a pause.
renew.banner.trialUrgent: Your free trial ends in {days} day(s) — renew today to keep posting.
renew.banner.graceLeft: {days} days of grace left before the shop becomes read-only.
renew.banner.suspendedRemedy: To restore posting, submit the plan payment from Settings or contact the platform.
platform.title: Platform console
platform.deniedBody: This section belongs to the platform team. It opens only with a platform admin grant — shop accounts, including shop owners, do not open it.
platform.signInPrompt: Sign in with an admin account to continue.
platform.demoBody: The platform console runs on the live platform only — demo mode has no businesses to administer.
platform.act.compTrial: Complimentary trial (comp) — logged as a comp act
platform.act.disagree: The counter and the platform figures disagree. Check before enforcing — enforcing a disagreeing counter as-is can refuse a healthy shop's postings.
platform.act.confirmDisagree: I checked the figures — flip anyway
platform.act.done: Done — the act and its event were recorded.
platform.act.failed: The act failed. Nothing was written.
platform.cfg.title: Payment instructions
platform.cfg.intro: What shopkeepers see on the renewal surface: where to send plan payments, and how to reach support. Display text only — there is no gateway behind it.
platform.admins.title: Platform admins
platform.admins.lastNote: The last admin cannot be revoked.
store.title: Online Store
store.subtitle: Your shop on the web: a published catalogue your customers can order from. Orders land in an inbox here and become ordinary sale orders — nothing is sold, and no money moves, until you convert an order.
store.state.darkPlan: Your store is hidden: the online store is part of the Advanced plan, and your current plan does not include it. Your published page and slug are kept — upgrading brings the store straight back.
store.state.darkState: Your store is hidden while your plan is {state}. Your published page and slug are kept — renewing brings the store straight back.
store.state.noPlan: Publishing needs a registered business. Once this shop has a plan, its store can go live here.
store.slugHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Customers will see this in your store link.
store.slugImmutable: Claimed — this link name never changes, so printed links keep working.
store.slugError.bad-chars: Only lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens.
store.slugError.reserved: That name is reserved — please pick another.
store.taglinePh: e.g. Fresh groceries, delivered in Farooka
store.noticePh: e.g. Orders placed after 8 pm are confirmed the next morning.
store.productsHelp: Tick what the world may see. Prices and stock bands refresh every time you publish; stock is always shown as a band, never a count.
store.autoRepublish: Update the store automatically when products change
store.unpublishedOk: Store switched off — the page and order intake are closed.
store.qrCaption: Print this code and keep it at the counter — customers scan it to open your store.
store.demoNote: This is the demo: publishing is off, and the store preview below is built from this device's demo data. No page is public and no order can be placed.
store.inboxEmpty: No store orders yet. Orders placed on your public store land here, ready to convert.
store.customerNew: No matching customer — converting creates one from this order.
store.driftTitle: Price check at today's live prices
store.driftNote: Orders always convert at today's live prices. Any difference from the published price is shown here, before you confirm — the customer hears the confirmed price from you.
store.drift.missing: This product has been deleted — its line is dropped.
store.convertFailed: That order could not be converted — it may already be handled.
shop.unavailableBody: The shop may have moved or switched its store off. Please check the link, or contact the shop directly.
shop.cartEmpty: Your order is empty — add something you need.
shop.priceNote: Prices are confirmed by the shop when it confirms your order.
shop.consentLabel: I agree to receive marketing messages from this shop on WhatsApp
shop.orderPlacedBody: The shop has your order and will confirm it with you, usually on WhatsApp. Nothing is charged until the shop confirms.
shop.errPhone: That phone number doesn't look right.
shop.errSend: The order couldn't be sent. Please try again, or message the shop on WhatsApp.
print.storeLink.caption: Order online from our store
wa.title: WhatsApp Marketing
wa.subtitle: Campaigns to your own customers, from your own WhatsApp number, sent by your own hand. Dukaan AI organises the consent, the lists and the record — the sending stays yours.
wa.lockedTitle: WhatsApp marketing is not in your plan
wa.lockedBody: Campaigns, templates and service reminders join the Standard plan. Your customers and their consent choices stay exactly as they are — upgrade to start sending.
wa.sendingPaused: Your plan is not active right now, so launching and sending are paused. Everything here stays readable — renew to send again.
wa.limits.title: How sending works — please read
wa.limits.body: Messages go one by one from your own WhatsApp: tap Send, the chat opens with the message ready, you press send there and come back. Nothing is sent automatically or in bulk, and this app cannot see whether a message was delivered or read — “sent” in the log means you confirmed you sent it. Only customers who agreed receive campaigns, and sending too many messages too fast can get a number restricted by WhatsApp — the one-by-one pace is the protection.
wa.suggest.title: Suggested reminders
wa.suggest.sub: Work your own data is pointing at today. Counts include only customers who agreed to WhatsApp marketing — starting a campaign is always your tap, never automatic.
wa.suggest.serviceSub: {count} customers · last job over {days} days ago
wa.serviceInterval.label: Service reminder interval (days)
wa.serviceInterval.sub: A delivered job older than this suggests a service reminder. Set by the owner.
wa.tpl.title: Message templates
wa.tpl.sub: Your own words, reused. Placeholders fill in per customer when the queue reaches them.
wa.tpl.placeholders: Placeholders: {name} the customer's name · {shop} your shop's name · {points} their loyalty points · {amount} their outstanding udhaar in rupees
wa.tpl.name: Template name
wa.tpl.bodyPh: Write the message your customers will receive…
wa.tpl.deleteSure: Delete this template? Campaigns already sent keep their record.
wa.tpl.empty: No templates yet. Write one, or start from a starter below.
wa.tpl.starters: Starter templates — copy, then make them yours
wa.tpl.starterPromo1: Assalam-o-Alaikum {name}, a special offer at {shop} this week — visit us and save on your regular shopping. Reply STOP to opt out.
wa.tpl.starterPromo2: Assalam-o-Alaikum {name}, fresh stock has arrived at {shop}. Come by while it lasts — and you have {points} loyalty points waiting to spend.
wa.tpl.starterReminder1: Assalam-o-Alaikum {name}, a gentle reminder from {shop}: Rs {amount} is outstanding on your account. Please clear it when convenient — thank you.
wa.tpl.starterReminder2: Assalam-o-Alaikum {name}, you have {points} loyalty points at {shop} that expire soon. Use them on your next visit so they are not lost.
wa.camp.title: Campaigns
wa.camp.sub: A campaign is a template plus an audience. The audience is worked out live when you launch — never a frozen list.
wa.camp.name: Campaign name
wa.camp.empty: No campaigns yet. Create one from a template and an audience.
wa.queue.title: Send queue
wa.queue.sub: One customer at a time. Open the chat, send in WhatsApp, come back and confirm.
wa.queue.honestNote: “Sent” here means you confirm you sent it in WhatsApp — this app cannot see delivery or reads, and does not pretend to.
wa.queue.done: This queue is finished — every recipient has a result in the log.
wa.queue.skippedOptout: Skipped: this customer is no longer opted in.
wa.queue.skippedInvalid: Skipped: this number does not look valid for WhatsApp.
wa.consent.label: This customer agrees to receive marketing messages on WhatsApp
wa.consent.sub: Only customers who agree get campaign messages. Bills, receipts and order updates are not marketing and can always be sent.
wa.consent.storefrontLabel: Customer agreed to WhatsApp marketing messages
wa.consent.storefrontSub: Tick only when the customer has agreed — the consent is recorded on their customer record as this order converts.
demo.addBody: Your business is empty. The demo set below will be added so you can explore every screen with realistic data. It never mixes with real books: once you trade for real, demo data can no longer be added.
demo.preListTitle: This demo set will be added
demo.addedBody: Added: {products} products, {customers} customers, {suppliers} suppliers, {sales} sales rows, {journal} journal entries.
demo.reAddBody: This wipes the current demo data and adds a fresh demo set. Your real data is never touched — this action is refused if the business holds any real record.
demo.refusedReal: Demo data cannot be added: this business already holds real records. Clear the business first if you want to start over.
demo.refusedMixed: Demo data cannot be re-added: the business holds real records alongside the demo set. Clear the business first if you want to start over.
demo.addFailed: Could not add demo data. Please try again.
trash.dangerSub: These actions change the whole business. They are owner-only and PIN-gated.
trash.clearBody: Everything in this business — bills, stock, customers, journal, the lot — is snapshotted into trash first, then wiped. The trash snapshot stays restorable for 30 days. Your shop profile, team and plan are NOT cleared.
trash.cleared: Business cleared. The snapshot is in trash until {date}.
trash.clearFailed: Could not clear the business. Nothing was wiped.
trash.replaceWarning: Warning: an active trash snapshot already exists. Clearing again will DELETE it permanently — it cannot be restored afterwards.
trash.title: Trash
trash.restoreDone: Restored. The business now holds the trashed books exactly.
trash.restoreRefused: Restore refused: the business is no longer empty. New data must be cleared first — a restore never merges.
trash.restoreExpired: This trash snapshot has expired and can no longer be restored.
trash.storefrontNote: Note: a published storefront is not cleared with the business. Unpublish it from the storefront screen if you no longer want it public.
trash.sweepNote: Expired snapshots are deleted when this panel opens.
